issues.legal_issue: A portion of an occupied main residential house used by the judgment debtor for the debtor’s own business remains part of the residential house for purposes of exemption from attachment.
material_facts: The judgment debtors occupied the building as their main residential house.
They used a portion of the building as a shop themselves.
The building’s residential and business uses did not make it two distinct buildings.
issues.conclusion: The portion used as a shop remained part of the main residential house, and the whole building was exempt from attachment.
issues.legal_principle: Clause (ccc) of the proviso to Section 60(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, added by the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 and amended by Punjab Acts 12 of 1940 and 6 of 1942, exempts a qualifying judgment debtor’s occupied main residential house, subject to the statutory exception for property specifically charged with the debt. A portion used by the debtor for the debtor’s own business does not thereby cease to be part of the residential house. The Court followed Firm Ganga Ram v. Firm Jia Ram, agreed with the relevant reasoning in Agha Jafar Ali Khan v. Radha Kishore, and distinguished the rule in Ude Bhan v. Kapoor Chand concerning a portion let to a tenant; it also referred to Punjab Mercantile Bank Ltd. v. Messrs General Typewriter Co.

rule.if: attachment_exemption_proceeding and main_residential_house and debtor_occupies_house and portion_occupied_by_debtor_for_business

predicates.attachment_exemption_proceeding: A judgment debtor seeks to prevent property from being taken or attached on the ground that it is a protected residence.
predicates.main_residential_house: The building is the judgment debtor’s main residential house.
predicates.debtor_occupies_house: The judgment debtor occupies the house.
predicates.portion_occupied_by_debtor_for_business: The judgment debtor personally occupies a portion of the house for the debtor’s own business.
predicates.whole_residential_building_exempt_from_a: The whole building is exempt from attachment.

issues.definition: When a judgment debtor occupies a building as the debtor’s main residence and personally uses a portion of it for business, the whole building is exempt from attachment in an attachment-exemption proceeding.
